title: Section invariant
statement:
Use the purity coefficient conventions [def-pur-conventions]: the global field $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$, a prime $\ell\ne\operatorname{char}(k)$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with uniformizer $\varpi_E$, $n\geq1$, and $A=A_{E,n}=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n$. The finite coefficient stage is $\Lambda=A$; the stages $\mathcal O_E,E,\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$ use the coefficient constructions specified in those conventions. Let $B,V$ be finite-type $k$-schemes [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], let $g:V\to B$ be smooth [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms], separated [def-weil-proper-morphism] and of finite type, and let $s:B\to V$ be a closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion] with $g\circ s=\mathrm{id}_B$.

On the small pro-etale sites [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site], let $Rg^!$ be the constructible exceptional inverse image [def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image], let $Ls^*$ and $\otimes^L_\Lambda$ be the derived operations [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom, def-weil-derived-tensor], and let $\Lambda_T$ denote the coefficient tensor unit on a scheme $T$: the constant sheaf $A_T$ at finite level, the completed coefficient sheaf $\widehat{\mathcal O}_{E,T}$ [def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients] at integral level, and its rationalized or common-stage image at the field levels [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom]. Put $\omega_g:=Rg^!\Lambda_B$. Define the *section invariant* by the actual derived pullback
$$
 C(g,s):=Ls^*\omega_g=Ls^*Rg^!\Lambda_B.
$$
It is tensor-invertible in $D^b_{ctf}(B,\Lambda)$ [def-weil-finite-tor-amplitude]: there is $Q\in D^b_{ctf}(B,\Lambda)$ with $C(g,s)\otimes^L_\Lambda Q\simeq\Lambda_B\simeq Q\otimes^L_\Lambda C(g,s)$. Thus it is an object of $\operatorname{Pic}(D^b_{ctf}(B,\Lambda))$, the groupoid whose objects are tensor-invertible objects and whose arrows are their isomorphisms. No choice of an orientation or of an isomorphism to a Tate twist is part of this definition.

proof.text: Apply [lem-pur-varying-dimension-dualizing-inverse] to $g$. It supplies $\omega_g,P\in D^b_{ctf}(V,\Lambda)$ and both inverse isomorphisms $e:\omega_g\otimes^L P\simeq\Lambda_V$ and $e':P\otimes^L\omega_g\simeq\Lambda_V$, also when the relative dimension varies or $V$ is empty. The hypotheses are exactly the smooth separated finite-type morphism and finite-type schemes in the statement. In the finite-level Lean realization, apply smooth_dimension_clopen_partition, restrict its index set to nonempty loci, and invoke varyingDimension_finite_dualizing_inverse. Identify its finiteExceptionalInverseImage functor with sfFiniteExceptional by the mapDerivedCategoryCompIso comparison for the fixed intrinsic realization; compactification instances are proof-irrelevant.

proof.text: Define $C(g,s)=Ls^*\omega_g$ by [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom] and put $Q=Ls^*P$. The closed immersion $s$ is proper, hence separated and finite type, by [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-proper]. Apply [lem-pur-all-stage-ctf-pullback-unit] to $s$ and both $\omega_g,P$: it puts $C(g,s),Q$ in $D^b_{ctf}(B,\Lambda)$ and gives $u_s:Ls^*\Lambda_V\simeq\Lambda_B$. This includes the unchanged finite Tor bounds, a single bound for all integral reductions, and the rationalized and common-stage coefficient constructions. In Lean, use the finite preservation conjunct of preserves_ctf_and_unit and its reexported ConstantGeometricStalkUnit.finiteUnit. Membership in the finite-Tor category is invariant under the preceding exceptional-image comparison: transport the constructibility predicate along the isomorphism and compose each representative isomorphism in the Tor test with its inverse.

proof.text:
Use the tensor comparison $\mu$ of [def-pur-finite-pullback-tensor-comparison]. The composites
$$
 C(g,s)\otimes^L Q\xrightarrow{\mu_{s;\omega_g,P}^{-1}}Ls^*(\omega_g\otimes^L P)\xrightarrow{Ls^*e}Ls^*\Lambda_V\xrightarrow{u_s}\Lambda_B,
$$
and the same composite with $(P,\omega_g,e')$ give the two inverse isomorphisms. The comparison is ambient at finite coefficients, so no tensor-closure claim for arbitrary bounded inputs is needed; its higher-coefficient maps use compatible reductions and their rationalized and common-stage images. Both factors lie in the full finite-Tor category by step 2. Thus the actual pullback is in its Picard groupoid. Neither its data nor these inverse maps choose a Tate orientation. The finiteIntrinsicDerivedTensor model and intrinsicCoefficientTensor are compared by lem-sf-cochain-tensor-model-rigidity: restrict finiteIntrinsicTensorModels.comparison to the flat-term K-flat representatives and apply uniqueness of tensor descent. Compose this comparison with canonicalFinitePullbackTensor inverse, pullback of each inverse map, and finiteUnit. This uses no higher-coefficient coherence theorem for the finite-level realization.
